text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The Islamist justice ministry has launched an investigation into journalists and unionists over articles allegedly encouraging a military coup.
- A new law passed despite sizeable opposition in parliament cancels trillions of lira of debt to the state's loss-making social security institutions.
HURRIYET
- Islamist MPs have begun to talk tough against the army which has ordered the government to crack down on Islamist zeal.
MILLIYET
- Rebel government MP Yalim Erez says there are two alternatives to the current Islamist-conservative government.
- Domestic debts have reached $30 billion despite a $15 billion target set by the government.
YENI YUZYIL

- A state security court is looking into reported comments -- which he has denied -- by an Islamist MP who allegedly warned that closing down Moslem religious schools would cause more bloodshed than Algeria.
- A treasury-led committee will meet next week to map out a medium-term economic programme to improve the ailing economy.
RADIKAL
- An Islamist sect leader has been calling for the introduction of Islamic Sharia law in his sermons in a mosque.
CUMHURIYET

- Opponents of the Islamist-conservative government will file a censure motion against it unless deputy prime minister and conservative leader Tansu Ciller agrees to forming an anti-Islamist government led by someone else in her party.
ZAMAN
- Tension is on the rise between the government and the secularist press.
DUNYA
- The treasury will issue a $250 million Eurobond on Monday.
- The Privatisation Administration said it had received 33 bids for the sale of facilities owned by state tourism concern Turban.
